23713.overview:
Goat Simulator is a third-person perspective action video game developed and published by Coffee Stain Studios. It was released for Microsoft Windows via Steam on 1 April 2014, and ports for Mac OS X and Linux were released on 27 June 2014. Mobile versions for iOS and Android were released on 17 September 2014. Versions for the Xbox 360 and Xbox One were released on 17 April 2015, and for PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4 on 11 August 2015; these ports were developed by Double Eleven.

The game has been compared by the developer as akin to skateboarding games, but where the player controls a goat aimed at doing as much damage as possible around an open-world map, without any other larger goals. The game, initially developed as a joke prototype from an internal game jam and shown in an early alpha state in YouTube videos, was met with excitement and attention, prompting the studio to build out the game into a releasable state while still retaining various non-breaking bugs and glitches to maintain the game's entertainment value.

The game received mixed reviews; some reviewers praised the title for providing a humorous sandbox interface to experiment with, while others criticized the game's reliance on social media to popularize what was otherwise a simple and buggy product.

475185.overview:
Geometry Dash SubZero is a rhythm-based action platformer that syncs every move to energized tracks.
Geometry Dash SubZero suits players who want fast sessions that focus on timing and pattern recognition during offline play. It centers on short attempts that reset quickly, which makes it useful for commutes or breaks, and it keeps progress pressure low while you learn. The striking visuals pair with high tempo music to set clear cues for jumps and flips, and the controls stay simple so you can concentrate on rhythm. If you plan to download Geometry Dash SubZero, expect a focused challenge built around repetition and precise taps.



Key features that define the challenge
Music synced one touch gameplay
Geometry Dash SubZero aligns obstacles and animations to the beat so each tap lands on a clear cue. You tap to jump, hold to fly or ride, and release to drop, all while the soundtrack marks the pace. This setup rewards consistent timing and gives immediate feedback whenever you miss a beat.

Tracks by MDK, Bossfight, and Boom Kitty
The stages are built around songs from MDK, Bossfight, and Boom Kitty, and the patterns reflect each track. As the music shifts, the pace and hazard types change in step, which helps you anticipate upcoming sections without on screen text. Audio and visuals work together to signal when to commit to a move.

Practice Mode for learning sections
You can switch to Practice Mode to place checkpoints and repeat difficult parts until the timing feels comfortable. This mode lowers the pressure while you map out routes and get used to transitions. When you return to a full run, your muscle memory carries over and makes progress more consistent.

Unlockable SubZero icons
Geometry Dash SubZero includes a set of SubZero themed icons that you unlock by meeting in game goals. Customizing the cube or vehicle gives a small sense of progression as you refine skills. Visual changes do not affect difficulty, so your focus stays on clean inputs.

Offline single player with high replay
The game works without an internet connection and saves locally, so you can play anywhere. Short runs, quick restarts, and escalating patterns encourage repeated attempts until a route clicks. This loop keeps attention on practice and completion rather than long sessions.

481039.overview: Galaga: Tekken 20th Anniversary Edition was a fixed shooter mobile game developed by Bandai Namco Entertainment Inc. The game was announced on April 1, 2015 as part of the 20th anniversary of the Tekken series and was released on April 30 for the iOS and Android platforms. The game is a mild crossover with Namco's Galaga series, with spacecrafts replaced by 8-bit Tekken characters. As of June 30, 2016, the game is no longer available.

482431.overview: Granny Smith chases an apple thief on roller skates through obstacle-filled gardens, streets and other locations. Timed jumps, pole swings and breakable scenery combine physics-based movement with fast arcade action.

482450.overview: A fast platform game in which the direction of gravity is reversed instead of using conventional jumps. Switch between the floor and ceiling to cross gaps, avoid obstacles and stay ahead of a pursuer.
